lines.spoken: Last time, Shee-ro-kee-ya burned in the middle of a Christmas sale in nineteen thirty-two.
Which raises a question:

lines.display: why was a Tokyo department store selling *Christmas* at all?
lines.spoken: why was a Tokyo department store selling Christmas at all?

lines.spoken: Japan's first Christmas Mass was held in fifteen fifty-two,

lines.spoken: and a fifteen sixty-eight Christmas play near Nagasaki reportedly drew two thousand people.
Then Christianity was banned for over two centuries.
It returned with the May-jee era.

lines.display: In *1900*, the upscale grocer *Meidi-ya* moved to Ginza
lines.spoken: In nineteen hundred, the upscale grocer May-dee-ya moved to Ginza
and dressed its front for Christmas.

lines.display: Crowds came to look, and other shops *copied* it.
lines.spoken: Crowds came to look, and other shops copied it.

lines.display: By the *Taishō* era, newspapers ran the same stories each December:
lines.spoken: By the Tie-show era, newspapers ran the same stories each December:
Ginza's decorations are up, here's what to give.
Then, in nineteen twenty-six, the calendar changed.
Emperor Tie-show died on the twenty-fifth of December, nineteen twenty-six,

lines.display: and his memorial day became a *national* *holiday*.
lines.spoken: and his memorial day became a national holiday.

lines.display: From *1927* to *1947*, Christmas Day was a *day* *off* —
lines.spoken: From nineteen twenty-seven to nineteen forty-seven, Christmas Day was a day off,
so Christmas Eve became a night out.

lines.display: In *1931* a Tokyo paper said Christmas was coming to more than *7,400* cafés,
lines.spoken: In nineteen thirty-one a Tokyo paper said Christmas was coming to more than seven thousand four hundred cafes,
and dance halls filled.

lines.display: The word only *vanished* from newspapers in *1940*, as the war deepened.
lines.spoken: The word only vanished from newspapers in nineteen forty, as the war deepened.
After the war it roared back,
and department-store Christmas sales hit fever pitch.
Shee-ro-kee-ya's nineteen thirty-two sale had been an early sign.
